investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T19:40:40–43Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-level agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the shared first step for all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner called POST /api/agents. This prevented the createAgent() call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 808) from succeeding, so the probe exited before writing any required evidence. All three remote-agents checks share this same agent-creation step as their upstream dependency, which is why all three failed with the identical message. This is an eval-observed failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written by the runner.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are listed as missing, consistent with the probe aborting at the createAgent() call.

sibling.remote-agent-state and sibling.remote-agent-runtime: both siblings carry the identical 409 message and empty evidenceKeys, confirming the failure originates at the shared agent-creation step, not in state-polling or runtime-chat logic.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:104-112: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState in [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the creation call never succeeded.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Org-level swarm agent quota exhausted: the production org used by the eval runner has reached its hard limit of 100 swarm agents. Prior eval runs or real user activity may have created agents that were not cleaned up, consuming all quota slots. The 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota. The runner wraps createAgent in withCleanup (line 806), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup executed, those agents would persist and consume quota.
TERTIARY — The eval service account or org used for probing shares its quota with real user traffic or other automated processes, causing quota to be consumed externally before the eval runs.

LOW CONFIDENCE — Commit 57b077e (feat(analytics): rebuild metrics, #64) touched eval workflow files (.github/workflows/aura-observability.yml, aura-evals.yml) and is the most recent change to all three implicated source files, but its touched paths contain no candidate needles matching the agent-creation logic, and the 409 error is a runtime quota signal, not a code defect. This commit is a hypothesis only and is not supported as causal by the current eval evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T19:40:40–43Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-level agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation is the shared first step for all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner called POST /api/agents. This prevented the createAgent() call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 808) from succeeding, so the probe exited before writing any required evidence. All three remote-agents checks share this same agent-creation step as their upstream dependency, which is why all three failed with the identical message. This is an eval-observed failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

Prior eval runs or real user activity may have created agents that were not cleaned up, consuming all quota slots. The 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'.

SECONDARY — Eval cleanup (withCleanup) failed in a prior run, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota. The runner wraps createAgent in withCleanup (line 806), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup executed, those agents would persist and consume quota.
TERTIARY — The eval service account or org used for probing shares its quota with real user traffic or other automated processes, causing quota to be consumed externally before the eval runs.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-06-15T19:40:41–43Z with the identical HTTP 409 response: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner calls POST /api/agents to create a new remote agent as its first step; the swarm backend is rejecting every creation attempt because the org has reached its 100-agent quota, so no agent is ever created, no evidence is collected, and all downstream contract assertions fail. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval probe account's org. Because the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 841) calls createAgent as its very first action, the 409 causes an immediate abort before any evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) can be collected, causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with the same message. The most likely cause is that prior eval runs created agents that were not cleaned up, exhausting the org-scoped quota of 100 agents. A secondary possibility is that the quota limit itself was recently lowered or the eval org was reassigned to a quota tier that is already full.

investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner could not be reached. The stream never progressed past generation_start, so neither required evidence key (frameTypes, imageUrlPresent) was collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 907) issued an SSE request to /api/generate/image/stream, which returned a 404. The production-api harness resolved to an endpoint that does not exist or is not deployed at the URL configured via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the production-api runtime environment and the /api/generate/image/stream route; it is not confirmed to be a user-facing product outage because no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence. The root cause is uncertain between two sub-causes: (1) the harness is not deployed or is misconfigured for the production-api target, or (2) the route /api/generate/image/stream was removed, renamed, or is behind an incompatible version relative to what the eval runner expects.
